en: Catalogue of Items Brought Back by the Great Master Chishō from the State of T’ang,
Province of Tung-tao, Prefecture of T’ai-chou, County of T’ang-hsing, Mount T’ien-t’ai, Kuo-ch’ing Temple, in the Kingdom of T’aeng (Great Tang).

General Catalogue of the Pilgrimage to the Two Capitals, the Two Zhe Provinces, Lingnan, and the Fujian Circuit by the Bhikṣu Enchin of Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei in the Capital of the Kingdom of Japan, Undertaken to Seek the Dharma in Tang China.
He transmitted the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna sūtras, vinayas, śāstras, and biographies,
as well as the fundamental texts for the great dhāraṇī teachings and maṇḍalas,
and the writings on the Perfect and Sudden Teaching of Tiantai.
Including various commentaries, sub-commentaries, notes, and miscellaneous records, as well as catalogs of sūtras, śāstras, and Sanskrit manuscripts,
the total count from beginning to end is four hundred forty-one volumes and one thousand fascicles.
The ritual implements, sacred objects,
and so forth, total sixteen items;
their names and descriptions are respectfully listed below.
*The Expanded Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings from the Kaiyuan Era*, thirty fascicles in three volumes, compiled by the Śramaṇa Xuanyi;

*The Benevolent Kings’ Prajñā Sūtra for Protecting the State*, two fascicles, translated by Kumārajīva; composed during the Zhenyuan era by the preceptor Man of Chanlin Monastery and his junior disciple, the Ācārya Li Gao;
this sūtra was sent to Japan to serve as the basis for a long-term lecture; *The Dharma-Mirror Sūtra*, one fascicle, incomplete.
One fascicle of the *Amoghapāśa-sūtra*, translated by Xuanzang and Yan Fotiao; one fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Seal of Entering and Not Entering Samādhi*, translated by Bodhiruci;
one fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Most Sublime and Victorious Samādhi*, translated by Yijing;
one fascicle of the *Vaipulya Sūtra Spoken by Samantabhadra*, included in the Great Zhou Catalogue; and the *Mahāyāna Vaipulya Essential Wisdom Sūtra*, translated by Śikṣānanda.
One fascicle, upper volume; two sutras bound together: *The Practice of the Bodhisattva Vajramakuṭi* translated by An Shigao (one fascicle);
*The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on Entering the Inconceivable Wisdom and Virtue of the Tathāgata* translated by Buddhabhadra (one fascicle);
*The Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha* from the *Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra* translated by Śikṣānanda.
*The Scripture on the Ten Stages and the Practice of the Way by Bodhisattva Tiyun Banna*, one or two fascicles;

*The Scripture on the Adornment of Wisdom Entering the Realm of All Buddhas* translated by Zhu Fahu, one fascicle; *The Mahāyāna Scripture on the Summit of Mount Gaya* translated by Saṃghavarman, one fascicle;
*The Scripture on Making Images of the Buddha* composed by Bodhiruci, one fascicle; [Works] lost in the Han period.
Two versions of the *Bath Image Merit Sūtra* (Yùxiàng Gōngdé Jīng); the *Sūtra on the Meaning of Precious Contemplation* (Bǎosīwéi Yìjìng Guānzìzài Púsà Suíxīn Jīng), one fascicle;

the *Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva from the Great Vaipulya* (Dàfāngguǎng Púsà Shīdì Jīng), one fascicle translated by Zhītōng; the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* (Wéimójì Jīng) in two fascicles by Jíkāyè;

and the lower fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Supernatural Powers of the Bodhisattva’s Sphere of Skillful Means* (Púsà Xíng Fāngbiàn Jìngjiè Shéntōng Jīng) by Zhīqián of the Wu dynasty, which had not yet reached completion.
*The Sūtra on Transformations*, three fascicles (lower fascicle); *The Mahāvaipulya Siṃhanāda Sūtra* translated by Guṇabhadra, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Sun-Light Mahāyāna Signs Adorned with a Hundred Merits*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha’s Cultivation of the Four Dharmas*; and *The Sun-Light Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇi-citta Dhāraṇī Mantra*.
*Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Yijing’s Ritual Procedures for the Mañjuśrī-Kuṅkumāra-rāja Mandala*, one fascicle;
*Yijing’s Ekādaśamukha-hṛdaya-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Xuanzang’s Mārīcī-devī-sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Lost Translation from the Liang Dynasty:
The Seven Koṭi Buddha-Mother Cundā Mahāvidyā Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vajrabodhi’s Jñānolkā Dhāraṇī*.
*Sūtra in One Scroll*: *The Great Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Spirit General Aṭavaka Spoken by Tiyun Bore*, translated during the Liang dynasty (translator lost).
*Six-Syllable Great Dhāraṇī Sūtra in One Scroll*, translated during the Liang dynasty (translator lost).
*The Divine Incantation of the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Scroll Lower, *Zhītong Dàfāngděng*.
*Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Dharma-saṃgha Bodhisattva Śīla-mūla*, one fascicle;
Dharmakṣema’s *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra Śāstra Verses*, one fascicle; Yijing’s *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra Śāstra*, one fascicle;
Ratnamati’s *Prakaraṇāryavācā Śāstra Verses*, one fascicle; Xuanzang’s *Rājadharmas*.
*Nyāyapraveśa-śāstra*, one fascicle; Xuanzang; *Madhyamaka-śāstra-anuvyākhyāna*, two fascicles; Prajñāruci;
*Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, three fascicles (upper and lower volumes); Paramārtha; *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, two fascicles;
Buddhapañita; *Hetuvidyānyāyamukha-śāstra*, one fascicle; Yijing; *Pañcaskandhaka-vyākhyāna*, one fascicle; Divākara.
*Pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle; *Śatākṣara-śāstra*, one fascicle by Dharmagupta; [translated] by Bodhiruci.
The above belong to the Mahāyāna Sūtra, Vinaya, and Śāstra sections.

*Dīrgha-āgama Daśānuśaya-sūtra*, two fascicles by An Shigao; *Madhyama-āgama Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra*, two fascicles; *Catuḥsatya-sūtra*, one fascicle by Dharmaphala; *Lakṣaṇa-sūtra*, [translated by] An Shigao.

*Yizhi jing* (Sūtra on Relying on Causes), one fascicle; translated by An Shigao. *Gaocheng nili jing* (Sūtra on the Hells of Gaocheng), one fascicle; translated by Kang Sengkai. *Lishui jing* (Sūtra on Leaving Sleepiness), one fascicle; translated by Zhu Tanwulan.

*Shixiang sinian rulai jing* (Sūtra on Eleven Contemplations and Mindfulness of the Tathāgata), one fascicle; translated by Zhu Fahu. *Za ahancha jing* (Saṃyuktāgama Sūtra), one fascicle; translated by Guṇabhadra. *Ahan fenbie jing* (Ānanda’s Discernment Sūtra), one fascicle;

translator lost during the Wei and Wu periods. *Shengjian yuye jing* (Sūtra of the Holy Firm Yuye), one fascicle. *Longwang xiongdi jing* (Sūtra of the Dragon King Brothers), one fascicle; translated by Zhu Tanwulan. *Xingqixing jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of Practice), two fascicles; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu period. *Wu...* [text fragment].

*The Sutra on the Original Arisings Spoken by One Hundred Disciples*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa. *The Sutra on the Eight Unfavourable Conditions and the Favourable Condition*, one fascicle.

*The Treatise on Following Characteristics*, two fascicles; translated by Yijing. *The Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, fascicles thirty-four and forty; translated by Paramārtha. *The Abhidharma-hṛdaya-sūtra*, fascicle six;

translated by Buddhabhadra and Dharmatrāta. *The Saṃyukta-abhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, fascicle ten; translated by Narendrayaśas together with Dharmajñāna. *The Śāriputra-abhidharma-śāstra*; translated by Saṃghavarman and others.
The sixth and twenty-second fascicles [of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*], one fascicle of the *Bimbiṣāra-pratītyasamutpāda-dharma* translated by Dharmayaśas and Dharmagupta,
three fascicles of the *Saptati-vākya-śāstra* by Āryadeva translated by Huìjiǎn, and seven fascicles of the *Kaihuáng sānbǎo lù* by Paramārtha;
totaling seventy-one works in one hundred and twenty-three fascicles across both Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna.
Both were missing from the original temple catalogues;
they were obtained by requesting copies from Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai and Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou.

*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Attainment of Buddhahood*, seven fascicles, translated by Amoghavajra; *The Brief Extract of the Recitation Ritual from the Vajraśekhara Yoga*, four fascicles, [translated by] Vajrabodhi.

*The Traces of Vajra-Dharma: Prohibitions on the Hundred Transformations, One Volume; "None Can Conquer," One Volume; *The Exposition of the Supernatural Powers by Ucchuṣma-Vajra*, One Volume; Combined Volume of the Above Two Works;
*The Great Compassionate Heart Dhāraṇī of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara*, One Volume; *The Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Method of Vairocana-Samādhi*, One Volume, by Vajrabodhi;
*The Secret Method of the Dhāraṇī of Acala’s Messenger*, One Volume, by Vajrabodhi; *The Yoga of Mañjuśrī in the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, by Vajrabodhi... [and so forth].
*The Chapter on Benefiting Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Non-Empty Great Bliss Vajra Non-Empty Reality Samaya*, one fascicle;
*The Non-Empty Vajraśekhara Yoga Rosary Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Non-Empty Dharani of the Vajra Life-Span of All Tathāgatas*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Wondrous One-Syllable Vajra Uṣṇīṣa*, three fascicles; *The Non-Empty Vajra Bhairava Assembly Vaipulya Ritual Manual*, one fascicle; *The Non-Empty Atidurāruṇa Sūtra*, one fascicle.

*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Auspicious Goddess Amoghapāśā* (1 scroll); *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Boundless Gate of the Emergence of Amogha* (1 scroll);
*The Amogha-ṭṛi-samaya Sūtra* (1 scroll); *The Ritual Manual of the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of Amogha* (3 scrolls);

*The Sūtra of the Twelve Epithets of the Auspicious Goddess Amoghapāśā* (1 scroll); *The Index to the Eighteen Assemblies of the Amogha-vajraśekhara Yoga* (1 scroll); *The Amogha-vajraśekhara-vibhanga*.

*Śrī-paramādya-tantra-rāja-ārya-mañjuśrī-nāma-samaya-kalpa* (The Holy Position Dharma Gate), one fascicle. *Buddhāvataṃsaka-mahāvaipulya-sūtra-tathāgata-uṣṇīṣa-sitātapatra-anavatapta-hradānirgata-bodhisattva-parivarta* (The Flower Ornament Great Vaipulya Sutra: The Chapter on the Bodhisattva Emerging from Lake Anavatapta, the White Parasol of the Tathāgata’s Uṣṇīṣa), five fascicles. *Tathāgata-hṛdaya-ratna-karaṇḍa-mudrā-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Seal of the Jewel Casket of the Heart of All Tathāgatas), one fascicle.
*Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Vajra Life-Span Dhāraṇī), one fascicle. *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Great Peacock Wisdom Queen), three fascicles.

*Amitāyus-tathāgata-pūjā-vidhi* (The Ritual for Making Offerings to Amitāyus Tathāgata), one fascicle. *Mahāmegha-vṛṣṭi-sādhana-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Great Cloud Wheel for Invoking Rain), two fascicles. *Yamāntaka-preta-dhāraṇī-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī for Bestowing upon the Hungry Ghosts of the Yamāntaka [Flame-Mouth] Realm), one fascicle.
*Amoghapāśa-bodhimaṇḍala-vyūha-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Amoghasumukha-kumāra-sūtra*, two fascicles (or three fascicles);
*Padma-rāja-tantra-vidhi*, one fascicle; *Amogha-vajraśekhara-prathama-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle; *Amogha-mahāyakṣa-priyaputra-siddhi-vidhi*, one fascicle;
*Amogha-mahāsukha-vajrāmoghatattva-samaya-sūtra-vyākhyā*, one fascicle; *Amogha-samantaprabhā-mahāpratisarā-dhāraṇī*.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, two fascicles; *The Verse on the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī of Amoghavajra*, one fascicle; *The Ritual for the Recitation of the Holy Yamāntaka, the Wrathful King, by Amoghavajra*, one fascicle;

*The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of Mahācaṇḍa Ucchuṣma by Amoghavajra*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Vajrakumāra, the Holy Caṇḍavajra, by Amoghavajra*, three fascicles;

*The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Honored One Ekajaṭī by Amoghavajra*, one fascicle; and *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra by Amoghavajra*.

One fascicle: *The Sūtra on Mārīcī Spoken by the Buddha*, translated by Amoghavajra; one fascicle: *The Method for the Swift and Immediate Realization of the Kāla-rākṣasa-Aveśa*, translated by Amoghavajra; one fascicle:

*The Method for the Seven-Limb Recitation and Practice of the Great Vairocana*, translated by Amoghavajra; one fascicle: *The Concise Method for the Recitation and Practice of the Mahāvairocanasūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra;

one fascicle: *The Great Ritual Manual of Trailokyavijaya from the Vajraśekhara*, translated by Amoghavajra; one fascicle: *The Yoga Ritual Manual of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra.
One fascicle of the *Amoghavajra-śekhara-sūtra: The Practice Method of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja* by Amoghavajra; two fascicles of the *Amoghavajra-manjuśrī-jyotiṣa-sūtra* by Amoghavajra;
one fascicle of the *Amoghavajra-trisamaya-bodhicitta-śāstra* by Amoghavajra; one fascicle of the *Amoghavajra-prajñāpāramitā-bhāvanā-caryā-vidhi* by Amoghavajra;

one fascicle of the *Amoghavajra-rajña-prajñā-pāramitā-dhāraṇī-vyākhyāna* by Amoghavajra; one fascicle of the *Amoghavajra-avalokiteśvara-mahākaruṇā-siddhi-japa-vidhi* by Amoghavajra; [and] the *Amoghavajra-rakṣā-rāṣṭra-pati*.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, ten fascicles; *The Sūtra on the Empowerment of the Radiance of Vajrapāṇi Prajñā*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Painting of the Great Amoghapāśa Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī*, one fascicle;
*The Essential Method of Recitation for the Amogha Golden Wheel King Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle; *The Method of the Joyful Dual-Body Vināyaka of the Great Holy Deva Amogha*, one fascicle;
*The Yoga Recitation Method of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Amogha*, one fascicle; and *The Practice of Samantabhadra according to the Vajraśekhara Yoga by Vajrabodhi*.
One scroll of the *Recitation Ritual* (Niansong yigui). One scroll of the *Zhenyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings* (Zhengyuan shijiao mulu) by Amoghavajra.

One set of five hanging scrolls of the Great Maṇḍala of the Matrix of Great Compassion of Mahāvairocana; these were presented to the Imperial Palace. One set of six hanging scrolls of the Nine Assemblies Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu;

these were presented to the Imperial Palace. One set of six hanging scrolls of the Maṇḍala of the Nine-Crested Wheel-King Mahāvairocana. One altar surface for the Dharma Maṇḍala of the Eighty-One Deities of the Vajradhātu.

The section on the ritual procedures for the drawing of the paper patterns and the consecration of the maṇḍala consists of ninety-four texts in one hundred twenty-eight fascicles. Regarding the implements:

one five-pronged vajra for the empowerment samaya, one five-pronged golden vajra bell—these two items constitute the Dharma seal of transmission from the Ācārya; and four *karmavajras* and four *kīlas* for stabilizing the altar—these ten items constitute the section on ritual implements.
The aforementioned Buddha images, sutras, and ritual implements were all obtained through transmission at Huguosi and other temples in Chang’an City, the capital.
One copy of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in seven fascicles was punctuated according to the Tiantai system by the śramaṇa Liangxu. The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* was punctuated [by him].

*Fahua jing xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sūtra), ten fascicles; composed by Tiantai. *Miaofa lianhua jing wenju* (Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sūtra), three versions totaling thirty fascicles;
composed by Tiantai. *Fahua shuji* (Commentary on the Record of the Lotus Sūtra), two versions totaling twenty fascicles; composed by Miaole.

*Miaofa lianhua jing xuanyi lüeyao* (Abridged Essential Meaning of the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sūtra), one fascicle; compiled by Miaole. *Miaofa lianhua jing dayi* (General Meaning of the Lotus Sūtra), one fascicle; composed by Ming.
*Guang Miaofa lianhua jing kewen* (Outline of the Extensive Lotus Sutra), two fascicles; *Miaofa lianhua jing xuan yi kewen* (Outline of the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), two fascicles;

*Longmen Miaofa lianhua jing shu kewen* (Outline of the Longmen Commentary on the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle; *Miaoyue Miaofa lianhua jing xuan yi shiqian yuanqi xu* (Preface to the Origin of Miaoyue’s Sub-commentary on the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle;
*Pumen Miaofa lianhua jing wenzju* (Words and Phrases of the Universal Gateway Chapter of the Lotus Sutra), three fascicles.
Volumes 1–3: *Tiantai Miaofa Lianhua Jing Wenju Yike* (The Textual Analysis of the Meaning of the Lotus Sutra’s Phrases); Volumes 20:

Two editions of *Liangxu Miaofa Lianhua Jing Shuji* (Recorded Commentary on the Lotus Sutra by Liangxu); Volume 1: *Miaofa Lianhua Jing Wenju Zhupin Yaoyi* (Essential Meanings of the Various Chapters of the Lotus Sutra’s Phrases).
Including the aforementioned [works by] Shi Yun, there are eighteen titles totaling one hundred and two volumes.

All belong to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* section. *Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Mohe zhiguan), ten fascicles; produced by Tiantai. *Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā*, fourteen fascicles; Tiantai. *Abridged Version of Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā*, six fascicles; Tiantai. *Fuxing souyao ji* (Search for the Essentials of the Aids to Practice of Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā), eleven fascicles; composed by Liangben. *Ke-wen* (Outline of Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā), two fascicles; Miaole. *Yili* (Exemplary Rules of Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā), one fascicle; Miaole. *Da ke-wen* (Major Outline of Mahā-śraddhotpāda-śamatha-vipaśyanā), one fascicle; Miaole. *Zongli* (General Principles of Śamatha-vipaśyanā), one fascicle; Miaole. *Liang buque* (Supplement by Liangben). The above eight works comprise forty-six fascicles.

All [the following] belong to the Section on Stopping and Contemplation (*śamatha-vipaśyanā*): The *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, four fascicles; translated by Dharmakṣema. The *Profound Meaning of the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-xuanyì*), one fascicle; composed by Tiantai. The *Words and Phrases of the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-wénjù*), three fascicles; composed by Tiantai.

The *Outline of the Words and Phrases of the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-wénjù-kēwén*), one fascicle; composed by Tiantai. The *Essentials of the Chan Gate* (*Chánlín-chánmén-yàoliè*), one fascicle; composed by Tiantai. The *Oral Instructions of the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai* (*Tiāntái Zhìzhě Dàshī kǒujié*), one fascicle; composed by Tiantai.

*The Method for Contemplating the Mind while Reciting Sutras, together with the Text for Making Vows*, one fascicle; *Tiantai’s Treatise on Contemplating the Mind*, one fascicle; *Commentary on the Words of Tiantai’s Treatise on Contemplating the Mind*, one fascicle;

*Danchu’s Meaning of Contemplating the Mind while Reciting the Twelve Divisions of the Sutra*, one fascicle; *Danchu’s Brief Clarification for Beginners: Essential Instructions on Seated Meditation and Śamatha-Vipaśyanā*, one fascicle (also titled *Small Śamatha-Vipaśyanā* or in two fascicles);

*Tiantai’s Ritual for Supplementing Deficiencies in the Vaipulya Repentance*, one fascicle; *Miaolu’s Method for Contemplating Food*, one fascicle; *Tiantai’s Record on the Infinite Life Contemplation Sutra*, one fascicle.

One fascicle of the *Commentary on the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* by Decong; thirty-six fascicles of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* from Tiantai; nine fascicles of the *Tiantai Commentary on the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* by Dharmakṣema;

one fascicle of the *Profound Meaning of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* by Yuanhao, for which the original manuscript was incomplete; fifteen fascicles of the *Draft Revised Text of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra Commentary* by Danqiu;
fifteen fascicles of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra Commentary* by Danqiu (missing the fourth and thirteenth fascicles); and the *Golden Scalpel* by Danqiu.

One fascicle of the *Lun* (Treatise); five fascicles of Miaole’s *Ke-wen* (Sectional Outline) of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*; one fascicle of the *Ke-wen* for the Latter Part of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* based on Danqiu’s commentary;

one fascicle of Miaole’s *Zhu-ke-wen* (Annotated Sectional Outline) of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*; three fascicles of the *Shangyuan Hao Fajie Cidi* (The Successive Stages of the Vast Dharmadhātu from the Upper Yuan);
and miscellaneous sections of various sūtra commentaries and other works.

One scroll of the Stele Inscription for Grand Master Si of Nanyue; one scroll of the Stele Inscription for Grand Master Zhi of Tiantai by Wang Langzhong. These two stele inscriptions by Prime Minister Wang are currently visible at the Qianfu Temple, in the Multistoried Stupa Courtyard of the Right Ward within the city of Chang’an, the capital.
This was thus provided by the Chan Master Chujin, a disciple of the Bequeathed Dharma.

One fascicle of the *Separate Biography of the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai*; one fascicle of the *Stele Inscription for the Chan Practice Hall at Mount Tiantai in Danqiu*; one fascicle of the *Stele Inscription for the Chan Forest Monastery of Fulong on Mount Tiantai by the Liang Family*;

and the *Biography of the Sixth Patriarch, the Great Master of Tiantai, by Censor Chen*, including the transmission of the Dharma to the Master Guang of Jingxi Miaole Temple and the propagation by his disciples from various provinces.

One fascicle of the *Jiaolu* (Catalogue of Teachings); one fascicle of the "Stele for the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Ritual of the Great Master of the Tiantai Forest of Chan"; one fascicle of the *Tiantai Shan Xiaolu* (Small Record of Mount Tiantai);

one copy of the "Stele for the Restoration of the Stone Elephant Site on Mount Tiantai by Meng Zhongcheng of Yuezhou"; one fascicle of the "Record of the Twelve Sites of the Tiantai Monastic Complex";

one copy of the "Record of the Divine Donation of Cypress Wood for the Sūtra Repository at Danqiu"; one copy of the "Record of the Three Pavilions of Mount Tiantai by Fasheng"; and [the record of] the two late Great Virtuous Ones of Fahua Monastery at Tianxing Temple in Changzhou during the Tang dynasty, by Prefect Lu.

One scroll of the *Epitaph for the Bhikṣuṇī* (upper portion; three versions combined into one scroll); one scroll of the *Biography of the Late Vinaya Master of Great Virtue at Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai*;

These three items consist of: a Sanskrit manuscript in a palm-leaf codex from the Mahānālandā Monastery in Central India by the Tripiṭaka Master Mañjuśrīdatta; a Sanskrit manuscript on *bhojapatra* bark from before the Buddha Hall of the Mahānālandā Monastery; and a five-pronged small golden vajra made of refined copper with a finger ring attached to its handle.
All of these were brought from the Buddha-land in the Western Heavens to the Great Tang by Brahmins learned in the Tripitaka;
their journey spanned one hundred sixty-eight thousand li.
The journey was perilous and difficult to describe.
As soon as Enchin arrived in Fuzhou,
he met the Tripiṭaka Master.
I was granted the Siddham syllabary and,
concurrently, entrusted with three articles of Dharma-faith,
which were subsequently transmitted to my own country.
May these be perpetually offered as sustenance.
May all who see, hear, or rejoice in this merit surely encounter the same conditions for rebirth.
One staff from a *peepal* tree in India; one staff from *ban* rattan in Guangzhou; and one glass flask—one set of these three items.
This monk from his native land, Tianyuan Jue,
came over from the Tang dynasty in the fifth year of the Kaicheng era and resided for a long time on Mount Wutai;
later, he traveled to Chang’an.
In the ninth year of the Dàzhōng era, they met within the city walls.

They themselves, together with Yuánzhēn, managed the transcription of the sacred teachings and the painting of maṇḍalas. In the sixth month of the tenth year, they saw each other off, and together with Yuánzhēn, they arrived at Tāi.
As the late summer passed,
he went out for a journey in the autumn months and arrived at Guangzhou,
where he encountered merchants from his own country, including Li Yingjue and Chen Taixin.
I enclose the aforementioned articles as offerings.
These shall henceforth be provided by our kingdom for perpetual worship:
one fly-whisk and one staff made of *khajūra* wood from the South Sea. These two items.
The above six items were sent by the Venerable Monk Cunsik, a Great Virtuous Teacher of the Kaiyuan Monastery in the Prefecture of Fuzhou,
as a Dharma gift for Yuanzhen.
And the section on ritual implements and religious articles:

one scroll titled *The Catalogue of the Dharma Transmitted by the Japanese Monk Enchin of Kūseiji on Mount Tiantai in Taizhou*; and one scroll titled *The General Catalogue of the Japanese Monk Enchin, a Bhikṣu of Enryakuji on Mount Hiei in the Capital, Concerning His Quest for the Dharma in Tang*. The aforementioned commentaries, records, and collections of the Śākyamuni teachings from the Kaiyuan and Zhenyuan eras, as well as those of the Northern and Southern schools—including treatises, biographies, recitation manuals, images, and ritual implements and articles, along with their respective preceding and following catalogues—are all itemized and listed in detail as previously stated.
May it be widely propagated throughout the ten directions to fully convey the Buddha’s intent.
I humbly pray that by this merit, the Sovereign may be supported above,
and the myriad people be rescued below.
Vertically exhausting the three realms and horizontally spanning a thousand lands,
both faith and slander alike form the causes for perfect enlightenment.
May enemies and kin alike ascend the lofty and expansive vehicle,
reaching together the ultimate state of Mahāvairocana.
Recorded with reverence.

On the fifteenth day of the fifth month in the twelfth year of the Dazhong era of the Great Tang, at Mount Hiei, Enryaku-ji, in the capital of the Kingdom of Japan, the bhikṣu Enchin recorded this catalog of the quest for the Dharma, together with the seven-rank official Jōshō Nanman, his minor disciple Kensei, the ascetic Sōgyō, and Daichiku Zenkichi. This single fascicle of the *Gyōhō Mokuroku* (Catalog of the Quest for the Dharma) is respectfully presented to the Grand Chancellery of the Imperial Government, praying that a karmic connection may be established.
Recorded by the monk Enchin on the eighteenth day of the fourth month in the year of Jia-mao, the third year of the Ten'nō era of Japan.
